name: SISO Agent Runtime
summary: The provider-neutral SISO coding-agent application boundary: explicit configuration, safe host launch, profile composition, task control, checkpoints, bounded context, status, and runtime event contracts.

reading.subtitle: A small provider-neutral host boundary with explicit configuration, bounded context, checkpoints and status contracts.
reading.why: Runtime gives a coding-agent host a deliberate application boundary: configure the executable and profile files explicitly, validate the setup, launch argv without a shell, and exchange durable checkpoint and status data. Its six internal modules describe a focused experimental contract rather than the broader Agent Base warehouse, so adoption still depends on the selected source revision and the host's own capabilities.

highlights.title: Read the public boundary
highlights.summary: The README defines the clean extraction, its six internal module responsibilities, the excluded domains, and the experimental 0.1.0 adoption limit.

highlights.title: Inspect the machine contract
highlights.summary: The manifest records provider neutrality, the Node CLI entrypoint, explicit JSON configuration, argv-only host launch, and each module responsibility.

highlights.title: Trace the command surface
highlights.summary: The CLI source defines manifest, doctor, where, run with optional dry-run, checkpoint, compact and status, including their required input options.

relationships.context: SISO Agent Runtime provides the coding-agent application boundary used within the stack; Herdr remains the independently owned persistent workspace substrate.

evidence.summary: The Runtime host boundary is workspace-neutral; no private Herdr control plane or topology is embedded.

relationships.context: The retired Agent Base source warehouse is preserved as extraction provenance; it is not the canonical Runtime repository or a runtime dependency.

evidence.summary: The shippable application boundary was separated from the mixed warehouse boundary.

Installer, launchers, runtime extensions, application surfaces, nested repositories, package manifests, repository size, and dirty state were read directly. The shippable center is an application/distribution; the surrounding repository is not one coherent Work.
Clean provider-neutral Runtime foundation published with six internal module contracts, five passing behavior tests, publication checks, and explicit parity limits.

Pinned public README, runtime manifest, and CLI command definitions reviewed. The documented surface is an experimental Node.js 20+ provider-neutral launcher with explicit JSON configuration, checkpoints, deterministic context compaction, and machine-readable status; no feature parity or installation readiness beyond the selected release claims is inferred.
Public main matches the pinned clean Runtime extraction; repository tests and publication gates passed.
